You know that it's pretty hard to give a place like this five stars. Its purpose is purely utilitarian. But good gravy, you'd think that a place like this could handle large crowds. It shouldn't take you a half-hour just to get one item. nnThat's what happened to me yesterday. I would have been better off going to Cogo's or 7-11. I might have paid a bit more, but I would have been in-and-out in under five minutes. I prefer the Giant Eagle in Squirrel Hill.

From the moment you walk into here it's like someone has hit you on the head very hard and you walk around in a confused state the rest of the time you're in there. nnThe set up is ridiculous. I mean, who wants to walk around in the freezer section and then go through a smaller than usual end of the aisle to see, SURPRISE, the meat section hidden off in an area where they could have knocked down the wall so you didn't have to do a little dance to get to it. Aisles seem extra long in this store, you can tell that they worked with the space they had. It's like when you are half way through the aisle and realize it's too late to turn around because it's the same distance to the end as it was to the beginning of the aisle, but you kind of just want to give up and sit on the floor because you feel like you've been walking forever. nnHonestly, I only went here because I was at Target and didn't want to venture any further to complete my shopping.

As soon as you get in you want to get out as quickly as possible. nn You don't want to do any major grocery shopping here. For one, the prices are high. Secondly, this Giant Eagle does not carry everything you need. Who has time to run to another store? Just get your basic necessities here. nnAs for produce, it can be awful at times. Whenever I go to Giant Eagle Market District down the street, the produce is fresh and smells invigorating. However, at Shakespeare, you are bound to find produce with wrinkles, open areas, mold and fruit flies- being sold at the same high prices. I can go to Trader Joe's and find much better produce for less. nnA pet peeve of mine is the self-checkout lines. Two of them are express lanes for items less than 12; the other lane has a belt if more than 12 items are being purchased. There should be TWO LINES but for some reason customers want to form one long super line, which holds up everything. The staff rarely sorts this out. nThe customer service is average here and I don't expect it to get any better. nnI only go here if I have to grab one or two items. The best times to go are early in the morning or late at night.

nnUnfortunately Kelly, Melissa, and Jen were not there so I settled for whoever was free at the time. nnWorst trim of my life: nshe cut off over an inch more than just the dead/split endsnshe did not cut the hair how I described initiallynshe did not change the cut to how I repeated during the cut when I noticed she was cutting it straight across instead of curving it in the back, which does NOT mix well with my curly hairnafter retelling her how I wanted it cut, she compared this tragedy to deaths of family/friends and how I should get over itnthe beautiful long layers I had and wanted again are now choppy, medium layersnmy left side is even choppier than the right side of my hairnI fear straightening my hair to make this unevenness less evidentnnI regret tipping her because I understand how the service industry works because my minimum tip of 20% for all service people is undeserved for her lack of work. nnI want everyone to know how the only good hair stylists there are Kelly (who moved to Philly), Melissa and Jen. If they are not available, do NOT risk going. nnAlso, the Supercuts Oakland location is horrible at waxing eyebrows unless you are lucky to get the only woman of color there. nnWhile it was a $20 cut (after the 20% tip), I know had to buy biotin to grow my hair faster so it is more expensive to me in the end. I hope this proves helpful to all perspective customers!

We've ordered takeout numerous times due to proximity, and nothing has been bad, but nothing has been special. The general Tso's tofu and the Moo Shu vegetables are the best things we've ordered. The eggplant was soggy and not great. The portions are large. Nothing is particularly spicy even if it is mentioned as being spicy on the menu. nnPrice: Tasty is cheap. nnDrinks: N/AnnAtmosphere: Typical Chinese takeout place. A photo of every single meal they offer is on the wall. Located in the plaza next to Pizza Parma. Decent location for that end of Shadyside. nnService: The employees speak poor English but can usually understand what you are askingt/telling them. The food is usually ready for takeout within 10-15 minutes. nn(+): many options, cheap, ready quicklynn(-): food is nothing to write home aboutnnWould I go back again? If I'm feeling too lazy/broke to go anywhere else.

Before I continue, I will come out and say that all of the food was a little tough - the eggroll especially(As was warned) -  and the rice had some dark spots(I assume it was from the bottom of the cooking vessel). However, I will chalk some of it up to my mistake because I thought they closed a half hour later,  than they did, and consequently ordered about 10 minutes before they closed. So, Tasty, you get a pass on the ricennAnyhow, I ordered a vegetable eggroll($1. 50) and general tso's tofu($8. 25)(I've learned to accept my guilty pleasure). I ordered the general tso's extra spicy - it was not. Also, the tofu was in very large chunks, which has seemed to be my luck lately. I want surface area, and I don't want to have to figure out how to cut my food with chopsticks. I will say, though, that the sauce was very tasty - enough to seal the deal for a future order at this place. nnThe eggroll, as I said, was tough.. It tasted good, but it was tough, and small.. . This probably won't be in my future order, however with the $10 minimum I do need to order something else with my tofu.. . I hope the soup is good. nnThe lady behind the counter was friendly and was decent on the phone and didn't once mention that they were closing so close to when I ordered. Portion size was good, for the $10. 44 it cost me, I'll definitely be able to make a lunch out of what is left.

On the other hand, I wasn't expecting much, so I guess the place lived up to my expectations. I've been trying to think of a good way to describe their food, and the best I can come up with is as follows. Imagine a cafeteria pasta dinner you might have been served as a child away at summer camp, and you'll have a pretty good idea. In other words, the food is perfectly edible here, but boring, and nothing you would want to actually pay for. There was nothing disgusting about it, it was just extremely uninspiring. To be fair, I only tried the pasta, bread, salad, soup, and calamari, so maybe they have amazing pizza here.. . It's possible, although unlikely based on what I've seen. nnOn the upside, the service was friendly enough, and there were plenty of empty tables at prime dinner time! If you're hungry, you'll definitely be full when you leave.

I woke up one morning to find a note attached to my windshield to inform me that I was the victim of a hit and run. The damage was minimal, but after calling it into my insurance company, they directed me to come here. nnWithin minutes of me hanging up my phone with the insurance company my phone was ringing to indicate that Mikes was calling to set up an appointment to get my car in for an estimate. I set up an appointment that was convenient for me and went about my day. nnWhen I arrived here to have my car viewed it was quite the easy task. My wait was minimal, the staff were polite and I wasn't being jerked around. Within five minutes of them looking at my car, I was out the door and heading back to my place. nnUnfortunately, they did not do any work to my vehicle at this point because the police are still looking into the person that hit my car. But if we get to that step, I am confident that they could not do anything wrong in my eyes. If their body work for a vehicle is anything like their customer service, they are definitely one of the best places to go in the city. nnYes people, this isn't the best neighborhood in the city, but get over it.

I used the Geico express service - I booked the estimate and repair online for the next day. When I dropped off my car, they were expecting me, it took less than 30 minutes and every single person I encountered at the shop was helpful and friendly and showed concern for me. The damage was minor, and the repairs took less than 48 hours to complete. My policy provides a rental car, and Enterprise was there when I checked in with my vehicle and the rental process was streamlined and easy. When I picked up my repaired car, it was just as efficient and friendly. Getting into an accident is frustrating and inconvenient and costly but Mike's Auto Body made the process of fixing things and getting me back on the road into a good experience. I wish more businesses treated their customers like Mike's treated me.

During the adoption process the employees were polite and seemed genuinely happy for me. Shortly after the adoption, I received emails from a volunteer to check in and to inquire about how the dog and I were adjusting. A few months after the adoption, it became clear that the dog had some pretty serious anxiety and behavioral issues (please note that there is no way the shelter staff could have known about the issues while the dog was in the shelter). I contacted the shelter and they practically  bent over backwards to help me with the dog's issues. The dog and I participated in two sessions of behavioral classes (Lacey is wonderful and never gave up on my dog! ), consulted with veterinary staff, and received constant emails from staff offering suggestions and checking in to see how I was doing. In the end, I learned how to manage the dog's behaviors and I love the dog dearly. Nine months later, I still receive emails from the shelter asking about the dog and offering more suggestions. nnI would highy suggest adopting from this shelter. I understand that my dog is sort of a worse-case-senerio of adopting a pre-owned dog; however, this shelter will make sure you are happy with your adoption and literally will do everything in their power to ensure both you and the adopted animal are ok. The shetler staff care deeply about the animal AND the human's well-being!

He was in pain and we decided the humane thing was to put him to sleep. We went to the ARL and asked the receptionist there if we had any other options available to us. "Well basically the only thing you can do is sign him over for euthanasia" she said in the most uncaring, apathetic voice possible. We were heartbroken of course. "Go wait by that door and someone will meet you. " After a few minutes another woman came out and took the carrier. "I'll bring your carrier back out in a minute. " We said no, that's okay, keep the carrier. She said okay and took our cat to the back. And that was it. No kind words, no sympathetic gestures, no "Would you like a moment before I take him? " No "I'm sorry. " Nothing. For us this was one of the worst days of our lives but nobody at the ARL seemed to care, or at least have been trained to pretend to care, one bit. nnThey get a couple stars for offering a necessary service. But other than that, this place will only be associated with making a terrible day that much worse with their lack of caring or empathy.

nnI went to this one with my husband a couple of times to pick up prescriptions, and the vibe from start to finish is so weird. Let's start with parking, which is in a lot behind the store. There's not a lot of visibility to the lot since it is on the back side of the CVS. Being that it is a pharmacy, there wouldn't be a back door or windows, so the lot has a feeling of dangerous seclusion. nnInside the store, everything I saw told me that "this is a pharmacy that is in a rough neighborhood": shelves are only about 4'6" tall (presumably so workers can see what people are doing in the aisles); bizarre things are locked in cabinets with clear covers (regular brands of shampoo?! ); beauty items regularly updated, weren't (I, er, have a nail polish problem; some of the products were about 4 seasons behind and quite a few polishes were separated); it feels like there isn't enough room for the products, which are disorganized and crammed onto shelves (reference the odd shelf height limitation). nnIf you can spare the gas and time, there is another a CVS on Center Ave within a mile or so or a Walgreen's (Penn Circ S+Trade St. ) and a Rite Aid (Baum+Negley) within 1/2 mile.

I'm not a huge fan of it - I go mostly due to convenience. Their greeting card selection is kind of lousy - I don't think I've ever found a decent card here. I keep trying, every holiday or birthday, but every section is just full of duds. Also, a lot of stuff is locked behind panels that you need the employees to unlock. Like, razor blades. And body wash. BODY WASH? It drives me nuts that I need to ask someone to open that shelf for me. It makes no sense. Staff is hit-or-miss with friendliness. Some people are cheerful, and some act like they want you to go away. nnGood things - I love their coupon rewards. I guess that's for all CVSes, not just this one, but it keeps me coming back because I get mad style coupons like every other visit. And I had a good experience getting a walk-in flu shot from the pharmacy from the friendly (and quite attractive) pharmacist. nnI'm just not crazy about the vibe here. It just seems kind of depressing, with the stuff locked up and the smallish store with kind of a blargh selection. I would much rather go to other pharmacies, but you can't beat this one for convenience (for me, anyway). And they have a parking lot, if that helps you.

When asked to repair something, Rockwel Realty will do it on their terms and refuse to give you notice of when they will enter your apartment despite multiple requestsnnWhen asked to clean mildew, they did in fact clean it with bleach while also spilling bleach on my sheets and ruining them. When told about this problem and that the mildew returned they said it was my fault for not turning the heat up and that damage done during service is an inherent risk the tenant is responsible for and nothing could be done. Their solution was for me to clean the mildew instead of properly insulating the unit to prevent mildew. nnThe entire building also has severe electrical problems that causes all lights to be replaced twice a month. No permanent fixes are made to existing units, but there is constant construction to expand an old building so they can collect more rent.

It took me far too long to come around and love Tazza D'oro. A horrible ex of mine loved this place and I admit that this soured me. I regret the time I wasted not going here. The dark wood inside comforts me. The small tables outside are a great place to spend the summer. nnTazza D'Oro brews Batdorf and Bronson beans (amazing), provides Enrico pastries (amazing) free wireless (amazing) and one of the most talented and friendly staffs I've ever met (amazing). Everyone who works there is *so* nice and *so* good at what they do. nnThey have a small menu of local/fresh food that looks amazing, but I have never actually eaten it. The espresso served here is actually better than the average shot served at Batdorf and Bronson locations in Olympia, WA. I talked about this with one of the barristas at TD'o and they were offended - "we calibrate our machines the same, we use the same beans, the exact same blends and milks and everything, it can't be different. " Sorry, Tazza D'oro, you are better. nnThe lines get long on weekend mornings, but they move quickly. There's a sense of community nestled here, just off the "main drag" of Highland Park, between Bryant st. and the reservoir. This is where you can pick up your CSA shipment for the week, where multiple weekly bike rides originate, where there are lively discussion groups meeting nearly every day. The percentage of students is low. Like the rest of Pittsburgh, there's a good chance you'll run into someone you know, but generally I see people I like and miss, which is different than the norm in Pittsburgh for me.

The espresso is, bar none, the best I've had - including my admittedly limited travels in Italy. It's stellar espresso - rich, thick, potent without being sour or bitter, with unique nuances that vary slightly depending on the shot and the weather, but are always fantastic. nnThe coffee is also terrific, and Tazza D'Oro uses Batdorf & Bronson beans - the best I've ever had for home grinding. They have a good selection of pastries and cookies, as well as a broad selection of tasty sandwiches that come with a satisfying side salad. nnIn addition, they have a wonderful selection of teas; I'm no expert, and don't know their supplier, but the half-dozen different blends I've tried were all memorably flavorful. nnAll that, and it's a lovely center of community, where you can bring your laptop or a book or a friend and spend the day. No one is rushed out the door, and there almost always seems to be a little room for your studies or conversation.

nnEnrico's Tazza D'oro Cafe is definitely very good--I love the location in Highland Park, and the early morning crowd seemed pretty nice and very eclectic. We even ran in to a friend while we were there and had a nice chat. nnMy girlfriend and I ordered lattes which were excellent--the space was overall very nice inside and while the selection of pastries was a bit thin I would say the ones they had looked good. I do wish they had more outdoor seating, though. It's tough to make the "I'm a fan" list for coffee houses. I'll try it again and may change my review in the future. nnWhile I"m on the note of Highland Park, I want to join the chorus of people who are dismayed by the recent hit and run involving the two bikers in Highland Park. Accidents (no matter how horrible) do happen, and as such I'm not as angry about the actual accident;  but to just drive away and leave people severely injured by the side of the road is pretty wretched behavior. At this point, i only hope that if you are the person who did this, you will at least dedicate the rest of your life to doing good to balance your to-date lousy behavior. nnIt's never too late.

nnSo here's what I liked: the cappuccino was perfect. It's an awesome cappuccino, topped with a cute foam art leaf. nnHere's what I didn't like: Sometimes I take my cappuccino plain, sometimes I take it with a shot of syrup. On this occassion I asked if I could get amaretto syrup, which they had. But the barista responded: "No, you can't. " He said they only make their cappuccino plain, and if I liked sweet, he could make me something special, but I would have to trust his taste. Here's the thing.. . I don't like sweet! I don't have much of a sweet tooth. I just wanted a tiny bit of sweet, so I didn't think trusting his mystery concoction was a good idea. I just got it plain. nnI'm not a big fan of coffee shop snobbery nor the fact that this guy seemed to have sterotyped me as a Starbucks-guzzling yuppie who had to be shown what a "REAL" cappuccino tasted like. Please, I lived in Italy, I've had a "REAL" cappuccino.. . but right now, I want a flavor shot in it. I still tipped because I wasn't sure if it was the barista or just a general rule at this place, and he did offer to make me something different. I just don't get what the deal is here.. . why do they even bother having flavor syrups if you're not "allowed" to add them to your drink? nnIt's a 5-star cappuccino for sure, but I had to subtract a star for the attitude.

Did I mention that I forgot my water bottle on my ride too? I was a desperate woman at the end of that one. nnSo I got home aired myself out and drove myself to Enrico's since a previous yelper mentioned she had the best iced caffe mocha there. There was easy street parking right out front and I really liked that it was nestled in the middle of a neighborhood and not a loud crowded street. Tables are large enough for good work space and folks had their laptops out inside enjoying the free wifi while the tables outside were filled with friends. nnSo why the 3 stars? Well the iced caffe mocha was a bit subpar. The syrup was all at the bottom leaving my first couple sips very watery. Could have been a better mix. Would I give this another try? Sure but I definitely will ask for a nice hard shake of my iced caffe mocha before taking a swig. nnThe coffee place at the Walnut Mall in Shadyside is still my favorite for the iced coffee of the year award. Try the iced OR blended ghiradelli mocha when you are shopping Shady-style - AWESOME!

I was a patient of Dr. Johnson until he left, and then Goldberg took over. Unfortunately, Goldberg shows a clear lack of empathy. His main focus is collecting co-pays and making sure patients come in every month just to renew prescriptions. He refuses to approve refills and disregards patients’ financial difficulties. Trying to get 90-day prescriptions through a mail-order pharmacy with him is completely unreasonable. On top of that, his office staff is completely inept. Most calls go straight to voicemail, which is never answered or returned. After dealing with this ongoing frustration, both my adult children and husband chose to leave the practice. The entire office acts as if they’re doing you a favor, which is incredibly aggravating. Avoid this doctor and his practice—you deserve much better, and they won’t be there when you truly need help. I’ve never felt compelled to write a negative review before, but this money-focused doctor left me no choice.

The office staff and administration were unprofessional throughout my experience. Although I left messages with several people about my bill, no one returned my calls. I had to persistently follow up just to get any response.

Most importantly, be sure your insurance covers Dr. Goldberg’s visits and blood work. He recommended a physical and knew I was a student because I informed him. I went ahead with the physical, only to later find out my health insurance doesn’t cover preventative visits. This resulted in an $800 bill for the blood work. As a student with no current income, I’m unable to pay this charge.

I’m truly surprised the doctor didn’t advise me to check if my insurance would cover these elective, preventative services. The office staff made it clear that it’s my responsibility to verify insurance coverage and that they cannot help with the bill. This whole situation has been incredibly frustrating!

My expectations for a driving range aren’t high—just decent mats, clean balls, and reasonable hours. With today’s ball-dispensing machines, you hardly need much staff, but this place doesn’t even offer that. It’s April and there are still no grass tees. They waited until this week to open for the season, even though we’ve had a month of perfect golfing weather. The mats are so worn and threadbare, they remind me of my 107-year-old Aunt Irene’s carpet.

As for hours, the range has lights but stops selling buckets of balls at 7:30 PM, while it’s still light outside. When I showed up, I honestly couldn’t tell if I was at a driving range or some kind of mastodon dig—or maybe a strip mine. There’s no grass, just mud, which does help you see how far you’re actually hitting the ball. And, to top it off, they only take cash.

All things considered, this place is terrible. The only real hope is that the owner sells it to someone who actually wants to run a business and take care of Pittsburgh’s golfers.

After seeing Rick Sebak’s “25 Things I Like About Pittsburgh,” my parents were eager to visit this spot, trusting his usually reliable recommendations. He suggested trying the Reuben, Fish Sandwich, and Open-Faced Steak Sandwich, so we headed there for a late Saturday lunch. We were seated right away, greeted by exceptionally friendly staff. My mom and I chose the fish sandwich, while my dad and brother went with the Reuben. The fish sandwich was very good, but the Reuben truly stood out—it was absolutely delicious. Both sandwiches were huge, easily enough for two people to share. Despite the generous portions, the prices were surprisingly reasonable: $8 for the fish sandwich and $7.50 for the Reuben. Our drinks were always refilled, and the staff checked on us several times throughout the meal. We’ll definitely be back! One thing to remember—they only accept cash, so come prepared. There’s an ATM on site, and it appears they’re closed Sundays and Mondays.

This place has been around forever, and its age definitely shows. If atmosphere is your priority, you might want to look elsewhere. But if you enjoy the vibe of a movie set in 1980s Pittsburgh, it fits perfectly. The service is inconsistent—most servers are good, one is notably slow, and one is exceptional. They’re all friendly, and usually several staff members check in to make sure you’re satisfied.

Because everything is made fresh, don’t expect speedy service—especially during busy times, your meal could take a while. Still, the food is truly outstanding! Any small complaints I have before eating vanish once the food arrives.

Favorites include the huge and delicious salmon fish sandwich, flounder, and shrimp prepared in various ways (though the “Norfolk” style is a bit greasy for my taste, and I never had it that way growing up). The Hawkins St Special and prime rib (meant for two, so be careful) also stand out.

With low prices, generous portions, and nearly everything tasting great, this place is a genuine gem. I’m not usually drawn to spots just for big portions, but if you want solid value without sacrificing flavor, this place delivers.

One Friday evening, on my way home from the airport, I decided to check out this spot—and it didn’t disappoint. It’s refreshing to enter a neighborhood bar where the music keeps playing and no one gives you the cold shoulder. The crowd was a mix of older hockey fans, young men in collared shirts, and thirtysomethings who’ve likely seen it all over the years.

The staff was excellent, though they seemed a bit short-handed and overwhelmed with orders that night. Despite this, my waitress stayed cheerful throughout my visit. There was also a waiter wearing a hooded cardigan that I genuinely wished I could take home—finding such a quality piece is rare for me.

We ordered a large white pizza, loaded with cheese, bursting with garlic flavor, and topped with spicy, savory sausage. Overall, it was delicious, but two things stood out: an excessive amount of grease (which I get is part of the deal but sometimes it’s just too much), and the mushrooms—canned mushrooms, no less. In my opinion, canned mushrooms are the worst canned food out there. I’d rather eat canned dog food than those. Even if they weren’t canned, they were still the worst mushrooms I’ve ever tasted. That alone is enough to knock a full star off my rating—truly revolting.

My advice? Keep everything else just as fantastic—the eclectic jukebox, flavorful food, reasonable prices, great crowd, and friendly staff—but please, upgrade the mushrooms. I’ll never understand why such an otherwise solid pizza is ruined by such subpar toppings.

I realize that small businesses often struggle to set up credit card systems, but could an ATM be provided instead? The lack of one has previously kept me from eating here.

When I scanned the usual breakfast menu, I decided on a tuna melt. Instead, I was served a cold tuna salad sandwich with a slice of cheese on toast. I ordered the melt specifically because I wanted something warm, but that expectation wasn’t met. The side dish was so forgettable that I can’t even recall what it was the next day.

That said, the dessert was a highlight—the cherry pecan pie was excellent! I haven’t seen that combination before, and it was truly enjoyable. The cherries weren’t the overly sweet canned kind but a tart variety topped with sugar, perfect for pie. It even inspired me to try making this pie with my parents during our next cherry harvest.

Overall, my first impression was just “Eh.” I’m still puzzled by Pittsburghers’ enthusiasm for breakfast. Waiting 30 minutes for a table at a small diner with a menu that basically lists “2 eggs and toast $x.xx,” “2 eggs, meat, and toast $x.xx,” and “2 eggs and pancake $x.xx” feels a bit much. Honestly, I’d rather go to Denny’s and order the “create your own Grand Slam!”

I always order my usual breakfast—eggs, ham, toast, and home fries—which is reliably delicious. However, the atmosphere has often been disappointing. The walls are dark, covered with autographs and scribbles from semi-famous people, along with numerous posters and photos of local figures. I secretly hope my photo will one day be among them. While it’s fun to take in all this at first, after several visits it becomes somewhat monotonous.

Today, though, I expected the same old experience but was completely surprised. The moment I saw the door, I noticed something different. The ambiance was noticeably lighter and brighter. To my delight, the walls had been freshly painted and new countertops installed. Although the renovations aren’t yet finished, the place now radiates a lively, cheerful energy. Between the excellent breakfast, the refreshed decor, and the five guys at the counter making me laugh, I know I’ll be back—maybe even for lunch.

My visit was somewhat disappointing overall. The food was passable—some dishes were better than expected, while others fell short—but generally just average. I ordered pancakes, bacon, and eggs. The pancakes were light and tasty, the home fries were unremarkable, and the eggs were poorly cooked. My son’s burger, however, was satisfying. The coffee stood out as a highlight, brewed perfectly, which I truly appreciated. I’d rate the food 3 out of 5.

Service, unfortunately, left a lot to be desired. Although our waitress was friendly, she seemed distracted and inattentive. We had to ask multiple times for coffee refills, silverware, and napkins. She also mixed up our order. For service, I’d give a 2 out of 5.

The interior had a touch of rustic charm, as expected, but cleanliness was lacking. Several ceiling leaks required buckets to catch dripping water, and one customer even tripped over a bucket and fell. I’d rate the interior 2 out of 5.

Prices were fair. Feeding my family of three cost $23 for breakfast, so I’d give the pricing a 3 out of 5.

In short, you can get decent food here at an affordable price, but it’s not an ideal place to dine. I’ll choose other nearby diners over Barb’s in the future.

Finding the place was simple, and parking posed no issues. Although it’s a "Seat Yourself" restaurant, there were no signs indicating this, so we stood there awkwardly for a moment. The waitress—probably Barb—was slow to notice us. She apologized, mentioning that a coworker had called in sick, which we appreciated. After bringing our drinks, she disappeared for about 20 minutes. We waited a full 30 minutes before she finally took our order, which was quite frustrating. I don’t mind waiting if the food is exceptional and made with care, but this felt like too long. We ordered the hot pepper omelette with home fries and toast, plus chocolate chip pancakes and sausage. The food was okay, nothing special. Eventually, a different waitress took over and was noticeably more attentive. We’re still undecided about returning.

I’m truly baffled by the glowing reviews this place has received—either the reviewers own the establishment or are recalling a time when it was actually decent. The atmosphere is rundown and grimy, with a strong smell of smoke permeating the entire space. To make matters worse, the bartender/server was extremely surly. We arrived on a Saturday night, eager to try the Irish dishes, but it quickly became clear that our expectations would not be met. It’s astonishing that a restaurant aiming for success wouldn’t have actual food available. Even before ordering, we were told there were no "pies"—no chicken pot pie, no shepherd’s pie, nothing. Undeterred, we tried ordering other items. My wife chose the Irish stew, only to be informed five minutes later that it was sold out, along with several other options for our group. When she picked a third choice, ham and cabbage, that too was unavailable. At that point, it was obvious the only thing left was whatever was crusted onto the menus. Frustrated, we asked for the bill for our drinks and left. To add insult to injury, they gave us a hard time for not having enough to put it on a debit card. In short, unless you enjoy your meal served with a large side of disappointment and gloom, I’d avoid this place like the plague. Speaking of which, thanks to Mr. Surly’s attitude, we left before things got worse—I only have two bathrooms at home, and I can’t imagine dealing with several violently ill guests at once.

Here’s the timeline: Murphy's Pour House operated from 1979 to 1985, followed by Sullivan's Pour House from 1995 to 2002, then Paddy's Pour House from 2002 to 2012. Now, with bagpipes marking its opening, Riley's Pour House launched on March 1, 2012. Still with me?

The place is a narrow, long bar, just like the classic Irish pubs of old. Smoking is thankfully banned inside—hooray! But sadly, the service remains as poor as ever.

This spot clearly needs an automated food and drink ticketing system. None of the cooks, bartenders, or servers seem to know who ordered what or which ticket belongs to which table. It’s actually kind of funny—unless you’re hungry or thirsty.

I really want this place to succeed. We need more Irish pubs and authentic local watering holes.

So come on, get it together, Murphy’s... or Sullivan’s... or Paddy’s... or Riley’s? Whatever the name, they have cold Guinness, Irish music, and a fun crowd.

The driver grabbed his cell phone but, instead of calling the number provided with the order, started dialing his supervisors and threatening me with felony charges. Taking initiative, I asked for the phone number of the person who placed the order, called my neighbor, and uncovered the mistake. Rather than offering a simple thank you or apology, he sped off—well over the speed limit on our street—to reach a destination just 50 feet away.

I thought about filing a complaint, but after reading other reviews, it’s clear the owners have no concern for Carnegie or its residents. On top of that, their food’s reputation around town is terrible, making a complaint seem pointless. I won’t be ordering from there again. Save yourself the hassle and choose any other restaurant in town.

We used a coupon from the paper for an 8-slice, 2-topping Sicilian pizza, but it was a major disappointment. The pizza wasn’t fully cut through, leaving four slices barely an inch wide while the others were about four inches—completely uneven. Toppings were sparse, with only around eight tiny pepperoni pieces scattered across the entire pizza. The onions came in large chunks, and the mushrooms tasted like they were straight from a can. The worst part was the thick, doughy crust, which had a strange fishy sourdough flavor. It was so noticeable that I genuinely wondered if the dough was spoiled or if fish sauce had been added for some odd reason. It was absolutely revolting.

We also ordered steak and Italian hoagies, but the vegetables were old and wilted, and neither sandwich had any dressing. The Italian hoagie contained cheap, low-quality deli meat with stingy portions. The “steak,” if you can call it that, was grayish instead of brown and looked like processed meat chopped up. It lacked any seasoning or flavor and had a texture similar to spam. It was so unappetizing that I only ate a quarter before throwing the rest away.

I’ve ordered from here before and have always been disappointed, but since I hadn’t tried their Sicilian pizza, I gave them another chance. That was a huge mistake. I will never order from them again!

When I check Yelp reviews, I tend to steer clear of the extremes—the overly positive and the very negative. Unfortunately, this office only has two reviews. During my first visit, the office administrator, who was very friendly, asked me to arrive early, before 9 a.m., to fill out paperwork. I arrived at 8:50 and waited, but two employees walked right past me, unlocking and then locking the door without so much as acknowledging my presence.

The door I stood by clearly displayed the office hours. After noticing the staff’s distracted or indifferent attitude—a concern another reviewer had also mentioned—I decided to leave. Later, the kind office admin called to let me know I had missed my appointment. I explained that several warning signs made me feel this wasn’t the right fit and wished her well.

If you do visit this dentist, I suggest using the front entrance farthest from the parking lot. Still, be aware that the staff’s inattentiveness, which I experienced firsthand, matches what others have pointed out. Overall, this was a disappointing experience for me.

The food here is fairly mediocre, but the prices are reasonable, fitting the profile of a low-budget Chinese eatery.

During my last—and unquestionably final—visit to pick up an order, I happened to witness a health inspector from the Allegheny County Health Department making his rounds. My food took much longer than usual, and while I waited, the inspector pointed out multiple violations. He also requested a certificate that the man behind the counter couldn’t produce. The inspector gave me a look as if I were crazy for waiting despite the obvious health concerns.

The place itself has always been somewhat unclean. The carpets are absolutely grimy, and the walls are no better. On top of that, children’s toys are often scattered across the floor because the owners’ kids are frequently there, so watch your step.

The staff seem genuinely kind and just trying to make a living, but when it comes to cleanliness, Don Don really falls short.

My parents have very particular tastes when it comes to Italian food, often driving to far-off places like Tarentum or Ligonier to find authentic, high-quality dishes. My dad, who can be a bit grumpy, is especially hard to convince to try new restaurants. The only reason I got him to this one was because they were already on their way to drop us off at the airport.

Now, my dad visits this restaurant regularly, which is impressive considering he lives all the way in Murrysville. The first sign he was pleased came right when the place opened at noon, a few days after Christmas—he genuinely seemed impressed. Then, at 1 p.m., he ordered wine, which is unusual since he rarely drinks before 5 p.m. That showed me he was really looking forward to the meal. The ultimate proof was the generous $20 tip he left on a $50 bill.

Even though I live in Texas now, I often think back fondly to that December afternoon. I had chicken piccata, which was absolutely perfect. My dad enjoyed eggplant rollatini, my mom had a pizza, and my husband chose simple pasta with marinara. Every dish was delicious, impressive, and affordable. In Austin, finding a decent Italian meal for four people under $50 is nearly impossible.

Pittsburgh has plenty of great Italian spots, but I treasure that day because it was one of the rare times my dad truly liked a place I took him to. :)

On both visits to Papa J’s, I was impressed by the banana pepper appetizer—it’s excellent and pairs perfectly with the fresh, flavorful bread and cheese served at the start. However, my girlfriend and I have had mixed results with the main courses. I really enjoyed the fish sandwich, but the eggplant parm sandwich was just average. My girlfriend ordered the salad with bread and basil, but the basil was overpowering, and the bread got soggy from the dressing.

Service has been inconsistent as well. On our first visit, the server went above and beyond, even making cocktail sauce for my fish sandwich. By contrast, the second time, the server seemed disengaged, was unfamiliar with the menu, and didn’t provide attentive care.

While I might return to Papa J’s, that last disappointing experience means it’s unlikely to be my top choice when dining around Carnegie or Robinson.

The restaurant’s charm was clear, set in an old brick building with large windows that gave off a cozy, neighborhood feel. On a Saturday night, it was lively but never felt overcrowded. Unfortunately, we were seated in a room with poor acoustics, making it difficult to hear both our tablemates and the waitress. Though she tried her best, the frustration showed on her face as she repeated the specials to both sides of the table.

Before dinner, some ordered bourbon on the rocks, which tasted watered down, while my lemon drop was well crafted. The bread was a standout—creamy is probably the best way to describe it. The fried zucchini was lightly breaded, not greasy, and came in a generous portion of two sliced zucchinis.

We sampled a variety of dishes. The pasta was dry, with too much pasta compared to sauce and meat. Those who had the fish special found it delicious, and the shrimp dish was also well received. I chose the chicken marsala, which was quite good; the sauce wasn’t overly thick, and the chicken stayed moist.

Desserts were questionable in terms of being homemade. The tiramisu and spumoni arrived in small, single-serving portions.

All in all, I was left on the fence about Papa J’s. “A-ok” sums up my overall impression best.

Our party of seven reserved a week in advance but was seated at the far back of the dining room, right next to a door where the constant clattering of pots, pans, and dishes disrupted our entire meal. Adding to the distraction, a Darth Vader-like hum came from the ceiling vent overhead. Our server seemed unfamiliar with several menu items, and three simple requests were overlooked: dressing on the side for a salad, less feta on one dish, and no oil on another. She blamed these errors on the cook but did offer to remake one entree. Additionally, when asked if we wanted pine nuts, feta, or Gorgonzola on our salad, we were charged an extra $2.00 per item on top of the $6.99 salad price, pushing the total to $10.99—an outrageous markup. Although the restaurant has great potential for ambiance, it falls short in both service and atmosphere. Given the quality and service, the prices are far too steep. I’m unlikely to return.

Our group of seven had already dined elsewhere earlier that evening. One of us approached the bar to let the staff know we were seated on the couches along the wall, as the place was quite busy. During his brief visit, a man behind the bar glanced at him but turned away without saying a word or alerting anyone else. He then asked a waitress who had come to the bar area if a server could take our drink order. She replied with a curt "yep" and abruptly walked away.

At that point, my friend asked to speak with the manager, who arrived a few minutes later. When my friend explained what had happened, the manager dismissively responded, "What do you want me to do?" My friend suggested an apology would be a reasonable start. Shockingly, the manager replied, "Get out and don't come back." Seriously?

My friend, well-traveled and familiar with upscale dining, stayed calm and polite, simply recounting the incident without any hostility.

Given this treatment, we left and returned to 131 East, where we had eaten earlier. The service there was exceptional, and the food and drinks were both creative and superb.

With several new restaurants opening recently in Carnegie, Papa J's is no longer the only choice. Unfortunately, this is how Papa J's management handles even a simple complaint—unacceptably. Do yourself a favor and visit one of the other nearby restaurants; they clearly understand customer service.

Failing so spectacularly really takes a special kind of talent. The cashier took my friend’s order but then completely ignored me. I had to push my way in front of him, even though he had already opened his register to help the person behind me. I waited over five minutes for a huge order that contained only one kid’s meal. Meanwhile, two people who ordered after me got their food first. When I asked about my order, the manager started yelling at the cashiers for “serving off their orders” without having the food ready. Yet, neither cashier was near the controls—the manager herself was the one handing out food and clearing the boards.

When the manager finally gave me my order, she was rude and didn’t check that I had everything on my receipt. She didn’t even apologize, despite my clear frustration with the poor service. After eating at many McDonald’s over the past 30 years—and even working at several—I understand bad days, bad moods, and occasional mistakes. But I have yet to have a decent experience at this location. It’s a place I’ll avoid unless someone in my party is dangerously low on blood sugar and needs to eat immediately. Maybe I should just go back to the racially biased service at Steak ’n Shake instead!

I used to come here mainly for the $1 iced coffees, but honestly, it’s just not worth it anymore. This McDonald’s is terrible, and most of the staff leave a lot to be desired. Every time I try the drive-thru, there’s a line of cars wrapped halfway around the building. Even when the line is shorter, there’s always some kind of delay. More often than not, I just give up and go inside instead.

Today was especially frustrating. I ordered an iced coffee—no cream or sugar—and a chocolate chip cookie. Pouring a coffee takes about 30 seconds, and grabbing a cookie is just as quick. Yet, I ended up waiting a full 10 minutes! That’s way too long for just a coffee and a cookie—I didn’t even order a full meal. Meanwhile, people who came in after me got their milkshakes and iced coffees in under two minutes. What’s going on?

When I asked the petite, sleepy-eyed cashier for a refund, she looked genuinely surprised, like I’d just woken her up. She said, “You’re the one who ordered the iced coffee? I can get it for you!” Seriously? She was the one who took my order! I told her I’d waited too long and just wanted my money back. The manager offered to remake the iced coffee, but I’d had enough and declined.

A few employees work hard, but most seem to be dragging their feet. There’s no organization or teamwork—everyone’s scrambling around like they don’t want to be there. I’ve worked in fast food before, so I get that it’s tough, but this was just bad.

Sorry, but I can’t recommend this McDonald’s. It’s a mess, and I’m not coming back. Looks like Starbucks is where I’m headed now—their iced coffees taste better anyway!

Our server, Annemarie, was clearly inattentive and brought us the wrong dish—one we never ordered, yet it still ended up on our bill. A friend ordered the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich, which the menu explicitly lists as including lettuce and tomato. However, the sandwich that arrived lacked both ingredients. When we pointed this out, the waitress simply brought a plate with lettuce and tomatoes on the side—how unprofessional!

After paying the full bill, I spoke with the manager, who didn’t offer any refund for the dish we never requested but were forced to accept. When I raised the issue of the missing lettuce and tomato on the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich, she claimed they had just updated the menus and that the sandwich was meant to come without those items. What a weak excuse! The online menu still clearly states the sandwich is "served with lettuce and tomato on a fresh-baked Kaiser roll." It’s disappointing that the manager chose to deceive rather than admit the mistake, blaming the new menu instead.

Not only were we charged for food we neither ordered nor ate, but the quality was subpar and didn’t match the menu description. To make matters worse, we had to deal with a rude waitress and a callous, dishonest manager. I won’t be returning to any Eat N Park location, nor will I recommend it to anyone. What a complete waste of time and money! Dealing with such indifferent and deceitful staff truly tested my patience that evening.

The baristas were genuinely welcoming, and throughout my visit, it was clear that plenty of regulars stopped by, chatting comfortably with almost everyone. The restroom was spotless and well maintained, and the trash bins around the store were all in good shape. While the pastries looked fresh, I chose not to try any. The noise level was ideal for getting work done—quiet, with music playing softly in the background.

However, I wish there were more seating options. Although it’s helpful that there’s a counter space at the end of the bar for solo workers, it doesn’t make up for the lack of tables. I suspect this is less of an issue in the summer when outdoor seating becomes available.

There was a treat receipt promotion happening, but the barista didn’t mention it, which seemed odd to me. Usually, staff will ask if you want your receipt so you can come back and take advantage of the offer. Today’s deal was a new pastry for $1; I know that in the summer, they offer $2 grande iced drinks with the morning’s receipt.

All in all, the environment felt warm and inviting—great for both working and socializing. It’s the consistent, friendly atmosphere I expect from Starbucks, and they definitely deserve recognition for that.

This store is packed with endless aisles of baskets, sparkling jewels, paper, and an overwhelming amount of scrapbooking supplies. But when I just need something as simple as felt, it’s a challenge to even know where to start. Always pressed for time, I rush in and immediately search for an employee—none to be found. If I shouted, my voice would only echo back. I weave through rows of paper, wood, and scrapbooking materials, but still no felt and no staff in sight.

After 15 minutes of wandering, I finally find someone. She’s very friendly and leads me directly to the felt. This isn’t the first time I’ve struggled to find help. When I mention it, she tells me they’re “low on payroll” and only she is allowed on the floor. Just her—the entire store! That’s ridiculous.

Less than a month ago, I was in a hurry again and waited about 15 minutes in line to check out. With two employees at the registers and six people in each line, I gave up and walked out.

Hey Michael, are you paying attention? You’re losing money because your customer service is awful—actually, there’s no service at all!

This store usually stocks the supplies I need, whether for cake and cupcake baking, icing, or scrapbooking. Compared to other Michaels locations, it feels fairly typical—just what you’d expect. It’s neither large nor small, simply a moderately sized store.

I really value using Michael’s coupons here because they save me a good amount of money. Instead of carrying paper coupons, I rely on the iPhone app, which conveniently offers coupons right on my phone.

The only downside is that checkout can occasionally be slow. Typically, there are only one or two customers ahead of me, so it’s not an issue. But today, even with just two people in line, progress was slow because one customer was having trouble with a coupon. The line grew longer, and although a couple of associates were nearby, they didn’t step in to help and kept calling for someone else. From my perspective as a former retail manager, associates shouldn’t just stand around near the registers without assisting customers. Whatever the reason, it comes across as rude and only makes everyone more impatient.

You’ll find supplies here for just about any craft—woodworking, painting, knitting, kids’ projects, scrapbooking, and so on. Still, if you’re after materials for your specific hobby, the options are usually pretty disappointing. The store is overflowing with cute and tempting things that make you feel like you have to buy them, and you start convincing yourself you’ll find a use for them. All this stuff makes the place feel cluttered. But if you walk in looking for something in particular, it’s a real challenge. The problem isn’t just tracking down the right aisle; often there’s nothing left on the shelves, or they don’t even carry what you need.

When I went in searching for crochet supplies, the yarn selection was so limited compared to other craft stores that I had to shop elsewhere. The prices are also noticeably higher than at other local shops. I tend to only drop by if I’m already at the Waterfront. Honestly, I’d suggest checking other craft stores first—unless you’re after glitter, especially fine glitter. Michael’s has the best range and quality of glitter I’ve found anywhere.

Steak and Shake perfectly captures the nostalgic atmosphere of classic diners, offering hearty meals at very affordable prices. One Tuesday afternoon around 3pm, my sisters and I dropped in and were pleasantly surprised to see their 2-4 happy hour sign right on the door—a welcome bonus! During this time, all shakes and drinks were half off.

I chose the Western BBQ burger, which included two thin patties, cheese, bacon, BBQ sauce, and fried onions, served with my favorite shoe string fries—all for just $4.79. Honestly, how could you go wrong? The food was genuinely flavorful, and I really enjoyed it. Feeling a bit indulgent thanks to happy hour, I also ordered a chocolate-covered strawberry shake. It was just okay—the artificial strawberry flavor was a little too strong for my taste, though the hot fudge definitely redeemed it. After all, hot fudge rarely disappoints.

In total, three meals and three shakes came to only $20, which felt like an amazing bargain. The food was tasty, and I had a great experience. I’d gladly return.

I really should have known better than to choose this place. I went through the drive-thru, fully expecting a wait since the sign clearly states the food is made fresh to order. Still, I ended up sitting at the window for nearly ten minutes while my meal was being prepared. During that time, I kept wishing I could cancel my order—and even more, that I hadn’t already paid.

While waiting, I watched the employees at work. The most unsettling moment was seeing the worker making the milkshakes. Although making a milkshake isn’t complicated, what disgusted me was watching him sniff several milkshake containers to check if they were clean instead of simply taking the extra time to wash them properly. After that, my food was finally ready, and I drove off.

When I finally ate, I was thoroughly underwhelmed. The fries were flavorless, and their thick cut gave the illusion of more than what I actually ordered. The so-called "steakburger"—which honestly should just be called a burger—was completely overpowered by the BBQ sauce; that was the only thing I could taste.

All of this has firmly cemented my decision never to return to one of these places again.

I once thought I understood Steak N Shake. I even had a small fondness for it—despite the salt and fat not being kind to my heart—because honestly, who can resist beef and drinkable ice cream? But after my last visit to this specific location, I found it absolutely disgusting. It’s been over a year since, and I won’t step foot in a Steak N Shake again as long as I care about my immune system.

After finishing my meal, I went to the restroom with two friends—because, well, we’re girls, and that’s perfectly normal. One stall was occupied, so two of us waited while the person inside took care of her business. But it quickly became obvious she wasn’t just using the restroom; she was also taking drive-through orders. Yes, really—“You want fries with that? *flush* That’ll be $5.50.” I’ve never seen anything so absurd as a drive-through transaction happening inside a restroom stall.

To make matters worse, once she finished her “bathroom break,” she walked straight out of the stall and back into the restaurant without washing her hands. She appeared too rushed to bother with hygiene so she could complete the order she had just taken. Meanwhile, I was struggling to keep down what I’d just eaten, fearing it would soon wreak havoc on my stomach.

In 2000, when the chain restaurant giant "Waterfront" opened, the parent company of The Rock Bottom Breweries decided to launch Sing Sing just behind The Brewery. At first, it was truly impressive. The very first house band put on shows that earned standing ovations—I was lucky to witness it myself. Their setlist spanned classics like "Stairway to Heaven," "Free Bird," "Stayin' Alive," and "She's My Cherry Pie," covering artists from Elton John to The Boss with remarkable accuracy. Even more striking was their ability to flawlessly perform obscure songs shouted out by the audience—tunes you thought only you knew—capturing the original bands’ sound effortlessly.

Nowadays, though, Sing Sing feels stuck in the early 2000s. The dueling piano act—where patrons shout out songs to stump the band or sing "You’re the Piano Man"—has clearly run its course. I don’t dislike Sing Sing, but I wouldn’t come here more than once a year. It’s definitely a “been there, done that” kind of spot now.

I’ll definitely be coming back—it was an amazing time! The admission was affordable, and arriving a bit early helped us snag a decent table. What really frustrated me, though, was seeing people reserve front-row tables and then never show up. Honestly, what’s wrong with those folks? In my opinion, everything! If you’re going to reserve a spot, you need to actually be there.

I have no complaints about the venue itself. The comedians were absolutely hilarious, and watching my brother get roasted repeatedly was the perfect highlight! This might be the only place where I actually enjoyed being around sloppy drunk people, thanks to comedians who take no prisoners.

I especially loved when Matt and Joey performed—they’re incredible and truly elevate the whole experience. They’re masters of their craft. I can’t wait for my next visit!

I had an absolute blast at the show. The dueling pianists were incredibly skilled, effortlessly playing requested rock songs while teasing me humorously throughout several numbers. After the performance, we headed across the hall to the adjoining "Rock Bottom" restaurant for some food. We enjoyed ourselves so much that we even returned for my friend’s bachelor party.

However, there were a few downsides. Since we went on a Thursday night, the atmosphere felt lacking due to the sparse crowd. With the place so empty, the musicians were a bit pushy about collecting tips. Honestly, it’s not our fault the venue was deserted on "Thirsty Thursday"—if their drinks weren’t so pricey, maybe more people would come. Also, the pianists occasionally used crude language, which seemed unnecessary because they were already hilarious. On top of that, there was no table service, and the only bartender we encountered was quite unpleasant. Despite these issues, I’ll probably return, but only for special occasions when it fits my budget.

In the past, I’ve had excellent experiences with Fran and the team, but this time was quite different. I called to ask about the cost of installing brakes and rotors I already had and was referred to Mark, the mechanic. I booked an appointment with him for Tuesday, September 30th. Mark initially quoted between $179 and $200, although the first person I spoke with quoted $150 to $179. He told me to bring the car in at 8 a.m. and assured me it would be finished the same day.

When I arrived promptly at 8 a.m. on September 30th, Mark either forgot about the appointment or hadn’t noted it down. He said, “Oh, I thought you were supposed to bring this by yesterday.” He then estimated the job would likely be done before 3 p.m. At 10:25 a.m., Mark called to inform me the charge would actually be $240—covering four hours of labor plus $13 in materials—even before starting the work to see how long it would take. He also said the car would be ready by 3 p.m., possibly earlier. For no clear reason, he added, “Oh, and we don’t take checks.”

Then, at 3:50 p.m., Mark called again to ask if I really needed the car back that day. I confirmed I absolutely did, expecting it by 3 p.m. or earlier as he had promised. He said he just had to finish one side and assured me it would be ready by 4:15 p.m. This left me barely enough time to catch a bus and get there before they closed at 4:30 p.m. Honestly, if the remaining work could genuinely be completed between 3:50 and 4:15, I doubt he would have asked if I still needed the car that day.

Because of all this, I feel he may have rushed when putting my car back together. Now, something feels slightly off with the alignment or the way the car drifts at times.

We waited two full hours for our meal, which included a pizza sub, French onion soup, fries, and buffalo chicken tenders. After an hour and a half, only the small pizza sub and buffalo chicken tenders arrived—but the tenders were made incorrectly, missing the hot sauce. The waitress admitted she knew about the error but still served them to see if my girlfriend would eat them. She didn’t and immediately sent them back.

Another thirty minutes passed, and we still hadn’t received the buffalo chicken tenders, the French onion soup (which should have been mostly prepared by then), or the fries. We were told the chef was new, yet no real effort was made to fix the situation—no complimentary appetizers or drinks were offered to make up for the delay. On top of that, the beer was quite expensive.

The food has always been mediocre at best, and the pizza sub was no different. After two hours, we left without getting about 75% of our order. I might consider returning because of their beer selection, but it won’t be anytime soon.

When I first arrived in PGH, locals kept insisting this was the go-to spot to watch a game, enjoy some brews, and get decent food. While that’s somewhat true, the negatives tend to overshadow the positives.

One clear highlight is their impressive new tap system. During my last visit, they had Thirsty Dog Leghumpper on draft, and it was spot-on. The system really elevates already excellent beer, and the selection is solid.

As a sports bar, expect loud TVs, plenty of shouting, and a crowd of intoxicated locals. I’m somewhat into that vibe, so it didn’t bother me. However, the staff clearly aren’t equipped to handle the chaos. Service is often slow, and the waitresses receive no training on the beers they pour. If you want to try something new, don’t expect any guidance here.

The biggest disappointment, though, is the food. I tried three simple dishes: a burger, a cheesesteak, and chicken tenders. The burger was cold and flavorless. The cheesesteak was passable but unremarkable. The chicken tenders were absolutely dreadful—the batter and portion size made me so ill I had to cut my night short. I managed only two out of seven tenders before giving up.

On a brighter note, their fries and wings are quite tasty.

Overall, Duke’s is a decent place to drink, but that’s about where its strengths end.

The entire environment is expertly designed to squeeze extra money from you—you’ll leave feeling both lighter in the wallet and noticeably heavier. Instead of straightforward pricing, you buy game credits on mag-stripe cards, allowing D&B to set arbitrary prices per game and keeping you unsure of your total spending. To make matters more confusing, drink and food menus completely omit prices: a Banana Split cocktail rang up at $6.05, and a Michelob was $3.40. Whether those prices are fair is anyone’s guess, but hiding them cleverly avoids standard pricing tactics like anchoring.

Meanwhile, the staff persistently pressure you to order dessert, while plastic dessert replicas displayed in the dining area subtly plant the craving as you walk to your table—a clever psychological nudge. The arcade games themselves haven’t changed much since my last visit to a D&B in California in 2002, still dominated by violent shooters and racing titles. They could definitely benefit from adding more fresh, innovative games.

All in all, it’s not a particularly pleasant experience, but at least it offers something different from the usual restaurant outing.

Walking into such a vast space felt unusual, especially after getting used to San Francisco’s typically cramped venues. Honestly, it was a bit unsettling. Dave and Buster’s is all about excess—sometimes to an almost absurd degree.

The food is pretty standard. Most of it is fried and, as another reviewer mentioned, not very healthy. You really have to dig through the menu to find anything remotely decent or nutritious.

But let’s be honest—people don’t come to Dave & Buster’s for the food; they come for the games. I’ve never been much into video or arcade games, but my brother and sister have always loved them. At first, I wasn’t sure I’d enjoy myself, but their excitement was contagious, and before long, I was genuinely having a great time.

Especially once I discovered my serious skills at Skee Ball and totally dominated. Trust me on that.

I was genuinely excited to return to this Dave and Buster's after many years, eager to dive into some games. I went with my cousins, and since none of us had eaten all day, we were quite hungry. Naturally, we opted for the Eat & Play Combo. Unfortunately, that’s where the trouble began.

Right from the start, we were greeted by a rather condescending hostess who led us to our table. Then the waiting began—about 25 minutes passed before our waitress, Ashley, finally came to take our order. We had plenty of time to decide, so we placed it quickly. After that, we sat chatting and waiting, surrounded by empty glasses. Ashley barely checked on us for refills, stopping by only once to promise she’d be right back with drinks—yet it took another 20 minutes before the refills actually arrived. Meanwhile, our food still hadn’t come, even though other customers who ordered after us were already eating. This was incredibly frustrating.

After waiting 45 minutes for our food, I asked to speak with a manager. A server responded rudely, saying, “Well, he’s really busy right now. I doubt he’ll be able to come out and talk to you.” Finally, 15 minutes later—an entire hour after ordering—our food arrived. Unsurprisingly, it was cold. By then, I was completely fed up and told Ashley how disappointed I was, especially after driving an hour only to experience such poor service. The manager never came to address my concerns, and we didn’t even get our meals comped. The only compensation offered was $10 in game cards. Big deal.

The games are the only positive aspect of this place, but even the prizes you redeem with tickets are cheap and worthless. In conclusion, I DO NOT RECOMMEND the Waterfront Dave and Buster’s in Homestead, PA. The whole experience was dreadful, and I have no plans to return anytime soon.

This place is great for eating, drinking, and having fun, and it’s open to all ages. I was genuinely excited when they announced that after 10 p.m., all children, even those with guardians, have to leave. That rule really sets the tone for a more adult atmosphere at night, which I enjoyed. Whether we play games or just relax, we always end up having a good time here.

However, I haven’t given it four stars because I’ve never managed to get a seat in the restaurant area, no matter when I visit. The food is the same wherever you sit, but I like the idea of enjoying the quieter, relaxed vibe in the restaurant, and I haven’t been able to experience that yet. On top of that, service around the bar tends to be a bit slow, which can get frustrating.

Overall, D&B’s is a reliable spot for food and entertainment. Just keep in mind that getting a table in the restaurant can be tough, and expect to wait a bit for service if you’re sitting near the bar.

After our visit yesterday, I can honestly say we won’t be returning. When we arrived, there was a long line of people waiting to buy game cards. Two employees were initially handling the line, but their pace was painfully slow. Then one left while the line still stretched out the door! The remaining worker was completely ineffective, taking an excessive amount of time to process each card. We waited over 20 minutes before being told another attendant was inside the game room. Unsurprisingly, the line there was just as long, with only one girl staffing the booth—and this was on a Saturday!

Finally obtaining our cards, we faced yet another wait to get a beer. Despite two bartenders on duty, the bar was packed, and it took nearly an hour before we could actually start gaming. The floors were filthy, scattered with trash, and the restrooms were disgusting. I used the bathroom twice, and both times there was no toilet paper—only TP strewn across the floor—and the sinks were far from clean. My boyfriend mentioned that the men’s restroom was equally bad, smelling strongly of urine with a broken paper towel dispenser.

All I can say is: get your act together. The crowd on Saturday was noticeably different from what it used to be, and I’m convinced it’s due to poor service and lack of cleanliness. Considering how expensive this place is, they seriously need better staffing on weekends. It’s a shame how quickly this place has declined, and we definitely will NOT be coming back anytime soon!

I want to begin by sharing my frustrating experience. Last night, I attended a post-wedding party at D&B—by the way, that’s a fantastic idea! Around midnight, the bar was fairly empty. There were three bartenders, but only one was actively checking on customers. The other two were chatting on the far end of the bar where no one was seated, which seemed quite counterproductive.

I waited for about five minutes. In a busy bar, that might be reasonable, but since I was the only one with my card out, it felt absurd. I made eye contact with one bartender twice and smiled, but she literally turned away. Eventually, I had to approach them to get their attention. Even standing right in front of them and smiling, they didn’t ask if I needed anything. I finally asked, “Are you working?” and they exchanged a strange look. I started feeling like I was the unreasonable one. I requested a beer and received it.

Meanwhile, another bartender brought food over and set it down. Then, right before my eyes, she took a fry from the plate and handed it to someone else on the opposite side of the bar. Seriously, what the heck? It felt like I was in some dingy bar in the middle of nowhere—not a reputable D&B.

That whole experience really left a bad taste in my mouth.

On a brighter note, D&B does offer a unique kind of entertainment when you want to mix things up. I remember coming here as a kid with my grandparents, and it was such a special treat! We’d eat at the restaurant and then spend hours playing games. The place holds some truly cherished memories for me.

It’s unfortunate that last night’s experience has tarnished the high regard I once had for D&B.

What’s not to enjoy about combining classic and modern games with food and drinks all in one place? The only potential drawback I can think of is the price. At first glance, this venue might seem a bit pricey, but they offer plenty of great deals depending on when you visit, whether you choose to "donate" to the Make-a-Wish Foundation, and if luck is on your side when spinning the prize wheel. Just be sure to check the deals ahead of time to get the best possible rate.

When it comes to games, there’s a wide variety to dive into. While ticket-dispensing games are always fun, my recent visits have gotten me two hours of arcade play for a very reasonable price (Mario Kart, anyone?!). All in all, this is a fantastic spot where a good time is almost guaranteed.

POSITIVES: The beer was dependable, and the pretzel appetizer brought a clever twist—soft pretzel chunks paired with spinach cheese dip. Portions were generous enough that most of us took leftovers home. The RB Appetizer Sampler was layered and plentiful, while the half rack of ribs looked as hearty as a full one. Service was attentive, with prompt seating and frequent refills of drinks and water. The restaurant’s playful name added a fun touch.

NEGATIVES: The menu was broad, offering everything from burgers and steak to chicken and salads, along with a wide selection of beers, wines, and cocktails. While variety can be a benefit, it slowed down the ordering process, and since the kitchen didn’t excel at any single dish, nothing really stood out. The food was decent but forgettable—I’ve had better beer, appetizers, and mains at many other breweries. The atmosphere was also quite quiet on a Monday night, with most tables empty.

In short, if you’re craving bar food, this place will do—but don’t expect anything remarkable.

These days, many breweries serve exceptional beer but fall short on the food, and unfortunately, Rock Bottom is no exception. When you visit a brewery, you expect the full experience—if it were just about the beer, I’d simply grab a growler to enjoy at home.

Speaking of the beer—EXCEPTIONAL!!! The Jagoff IPA stands out as one of the best IPAs I’ve ever had. The only one I might rank higher is Dogfish Head, but that’s a matter of personal preference. Their beer selection is always changing, with some impressive seasonal offerings. You really can’t go wrong; there’s bound to be a beer that suits everyone’s taste.

On the other hand, the food is unpredictable. Sometimes it’s excellent; other times, it’s disappointing. What frustrates me most is the complete lack of consistency. One visit, the food is perfect; the next, it may arrive cold, overcooked, or taste completely different. It feels like the food quality doesn’t receive the attention it deserves.

That’s the bottom line. If Rock Bottom could fix their food consistency, it would easily be a five-star spot. Until then, it remains a hit-or-miss experience.

The outing turned out to be just average—not quite better than TGI Fridays, but still an upgrade from Eat n Park. Here’s the full story.

My husband and I stopped by on a Saturday evening after a show at the Improv, feeling happy and ready for some good food. We started with drinks: he ordered a house-brewed wheat beer, and I went for my usual Bloody Mary made with Absolut Peppar. He thought the beer was decent but wouldn’t go out of his way to order it again—though, to be fair, he did get a second one “just to be sure.” My Bloody Mary was a disappointment: watered-down tomato juice with no noticeable pepper or seasoning. Even a basic mix would have been better. Our friendly, efficient waitress took it back and watched as another bartender remade it, but the second attempt was no improvement. That went back as well, so I switched to a safer choice—an Amaretto sour—which was fine and uncomplicated.

For dinner, my husband ordered a Reuben—though I don’t understand why, since they rarely measure up to the legendary version from the now-closed Gazebo in Shadyside (a place younger folks probably don’t know). He described his sandwich as “fine.” I chose the Texas Fire steak with jalapeño butter, which I really enjoyed. It delivered a strong kick of heat and flavor, but the sides were uninspired: steamed vegetables that lost all their taste and cheddar mashed potatoes that didn’t seem to contain any cheddar.

The bill was reasonable, especially since we used a Living Social deal that took $30 off, leaving us with just over $12 before tip. Not bad, considering the deal itself cost $15. However, if we had paid full price, the experience wouldn’t have been worth it. We’ll definitely keep going to the Improv—as we have before—but next time we’ll pick a different place to eat afterward.

The beer at Rock Bottom is fairly good, but it has never compensated for the consistently poor service and the food, which is unimpressive at best. Even ordering beers at the bar was a hassle. We first asked the women to try, hoping for better luck, but that didn’t work out. Then the men gave it a shot, and that also failed. If we hadn’t been genuinely craving a cold beer after a comedy show at The Improv, we probably would have just left. The place wasn’t busy enough to justify being ignored by the bartender, so I can’t overlook that. Spotty service at Rock Bottom has always been a problem, so this experience was no surprise.

Considering the weak food and poor service, along with Rock Bottom being too far from home for just a night out drinking, it’s easy to see why I’ve avoided this spot before—and why I won’t be returning often in the future.

It’s hard to say exactly how many years—perhaps even decades—have passed since my last visit here. Regardless of the exact timeline, it had been a long while. With a gift certificate in hand, I decided to celebrate my brother’s birthday with a dinner outing.

As I’ve gotten older, my patience for crowds and noisy children has noticeably diminished. So, I told my brother to be ready by 4 p.m., aiming to arrive at the Waterfront before the evening rush and the start of date-night crowds. Plus, the Pirates game was set to begin at 4:05, giving us a perfect chance to enjoy some beers while catching the action.

When we arrived, the bar area was already quite busy, but we still managed to find a table. Our server was friendly, attentive, and helpful from the moment we sat down. Eager to try everything, we both ordered the sampler. I appreciated how she approached with a full tray and said, “I have to go back for the rest.” In the end, each of us had 10 different beers in small glasses—probably 3 or 4 ounces each; I can never quite tell. Rock Bottom clearly knows their craft. I liked most of the brews, with only a few not quite to my taste. At $6.95 for 10 samples, it was an excellent deal.

While sampling, we enjoyed some Southwest Egg Rolls. They were okay—nothing extraordinary—and not quite what I expected, but the spicy ranch dipping sauce was fantastic. As our beers ran low, we each ordered a Kobe Burger, cooked perfectly to our preferred medium. To top off the night, the Pirates secured a win, making the evening even better.

My only real gripe as a beer enthusiast is the cost of the growler. The empty glass alone is priced at $12.95, which seems excessive. For comparison, East End charges just $3 for their bottles, and Penn Brewery $5. Paying more for the container than the beer inside strikes me as absurd, so I left empty-handed. Nevertheless, that won’t keep me from returning.

A colleague brought a coupon for a free mini appetizer, but the waitress told us they weren’t serving mini appetizers and instead gave us a full-sized chicken quesadilla. If you’ve ever had Chili’s southwestern egg rolls, the filling tasted just like that—I’m a big fan!

On Mondays, burgers are half off, so I tried the Just Hot Enough burger. It came topped with crispy jalapeños, pepper jack cheese, pico de gallo, and housemade habanero ketchup. It was fantastic! The ketchup really stood out, and the fries were perfectly crispy.

While lunch prices are a bit high, going on a Monday definitely makes it worth it. The food quality more than justifies the cost, but don’t expect to pay under $10 for a sit-down meal.

The staff was very friendly, and our waitress was attentive throughout. Service was quick, and you can easily get in and out in under an hour.

I’m taking off one star due to a few unfortunate issues; otherwise, this place would easily earn a solid 3. Our server was attentive, consistently refilling our water and soda.
